import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/training_3.csv"
]

# List to hold DataFrames from each source
dfs = []

# Load each source CSV, reading with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Extract only the 'TrackID' column as target schema requires only this column
    df_trackid = df[['TrackID']]
    dfs.append(df_trackid)

# Since all source tables have the same schema and target schema is a subset (only TrackID),
# we can union all TrackID columns from all sources by concatenation
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Remove duplicate TrackID values to match the target examples which show unique TrackIDs
# The target examples show distinct TrackID values, so we keep unique TrackIDs only
combined_unique = combined_df.drop_duplicates(subset=['TrackID']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Ensure TrackID column is integer type as per target schema
combined_unique['TrackID'] = combined_unique['TrackID'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_88/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_unique.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

# UNION all source tables (concatenate)

# GROUP BY TrackID to get unique TrackIDs (no aggregation needed)
